title: Shard key rotation + tenant-consistent-hash routing for ingestion gateway
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Problem: The current ingestion gateway assigns tenant logs to shards using a static tenant->shard mapping. As tenant volumes diverge (some tenants produce 10x the average tokens/s), we observe hot shards, increased tail latency, and frequent downstream tail-drop on Loki ingestion nodes. This ticket implements a migration to rotating shard keys with tenant-consistent-hash routing to reduce hotspotting and enable smooth tenant rebalancing across the cluster.

Goals:
- Eliminate long-term hot shards by introducing an epoch-based shard key rotation that rebalances tenants over time.
- Maintain sticky routing for low-latency flows while enabling gradual rehash during migrations.
- Preserve log ordering and idempotency guarantees for per-tenant streams.
- Provide metrics and dashboards to detect and alert on shard imbalance and rehash regressions.

Design summary:
- Routing: Use a tenant-consistent hash ring per ingestion region. Each tenant is mapped to a primary shard via H(tenant_id || rotation_epoch || salt) mod N_shards. Rotation occurs by incrementing rotation_epoch on a controlled cadence (default: daily; adjustable).
- Sticky routing: Ingress nodes cache tenant->shard assignment for 5 minutes to reduce churn for bursty tenants. Cached entries include epoch and a TTL.
- Dual-write migration mode: For epoch transitions we support a two-phase dual-write where the gateway writes to both old and new shard targets for a grace period. Downstream deduplication keys (ingest_id + sequence) ensure idempotency.
- Idempotency & ordering: Each tenant log batch includes a sequence window and origin_epoch. Downstream dedupe service (Redis with bounded TTL) dedups by tenant:origin_epoch:seq_range.
- Tracing/logging: Add ingest_shard and rotation_epoch tags to traces. Correlation IDs are propagated from edge through gateway -> shard -> Loki, surfaced as Loki labels.
- Metrics: shard_assignments_changed, shard_hotness_ratio, rotation_events_total, rehash_duration_seconds, dedupe_false_positive_rate.

Migration strategy:
1) Canary: Roll gateway change to 5% of ingress nodes with epoch rotation disabled; validate no errors.
2) Canary with epoch enabled for a small tenant cohort (internal test tenants).
3) Enable dual-write for 24-72 hours for a single region to validate dedupe correctness and downstream throughput.
4) Gradually increase rotation epoch frequency and roll out to remaining regions.
5) After 7 days with no regressions, disable dual-write and remove migration TTLs.

Rollback plan:
- If dedupe false positives or tail latency increases > 30% for sustained 10m, flip gateway back to previous static mapping and initiate incident runbook. Runbook link in attachments.

Testing approach:
- Unit: hash ring, epoch increment, cache TTL behavior.
- Integration: end-to-end ingest for synthetic tenants with controlled skew (0.1x - 20x baseline). Verify ordering and dedupe metrics.
- Load: k6 script that recreates tenant skew observed in production.

Observability and dashboards:
- New Grafana panels: Shard hotness heatmap, tenant rehash churn, rotation events timeline, dedupe hit/miss ratio. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ingest/shard-rotation-overview
- Tracing: propagate ingest_shard and rotation_epoch as span tags and add a derived trace-span filter in the latency dashboard.

Open trade-offs and notes:
- Rotation cadence: faster rotations rebalance quicker but increase cross-shard traffic and cache churn. Default is daily; ops can tune per-customer for Dedicated customers.
- Dual-write increases write amplification downstream (approx +1x) but is necessary for safe migration without data loss. We will throttle dual-write for high-volume tenants by sampling.
- Consistent hashing with virtual nodes was chosen to reduce rebalancing ripple but increases memory on routing table. We limit virtual nodes per physical shard to 64.

- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Shard+Rotation+Design+2026
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-gateway/pull/3124
- Load test repo & k6 script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-load-tests/tree/main/shard-rotation

acceptance_criteria: 1) Ingress nodes route tenants via H(tenant||epoch||salt) and cached entries respect TTL. 2) Dual-write mode does not drop logs; dedupe hit rate >= 99.99% for synthetic test tenants. 3) Shard hotness heatmap shows 50% reduction in 95th percentile hotness for top-10 tenants in load test. 4) No increase in error rate or 99th latency in production canary for 6 hours. 5) Observability panels show rotation events and rehash_duration; alerts fire for rehash_duration_seconds > 300s.
